title: AXAML: the markup
sub: Tags are objects, attributes are properties
cards/0/body: Each tag is an object, each attribute is one of its properties, and a nested tag is its content.
cards/0/code:
<Window xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
        xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
        x:Class="MyApp.Views.MainWindow"
        Title="Hello" Width="400" Height="200">
  <Button Content="Click me" HorizontalAlignment="Center"/>
</Window>
cards/1/body: Markup is just a convenient notation. You can write the same thing in code:
cards/2/q: What does the tag <Button Content="Click me"/> do?
cards/2/options/0: Creates a Button object and sets its Content property to "Click me"
cards/2/options/2: Calls a method named Click me
cards/3/q: Which line links the markup to a C# class?
cards/3/explain: x:Class says: this markup is the other half of the partial class MainWindow.
cards/4/body: Give an element a name, and C# gets a field with that name. Markup is compiled at build time, so a typo in the name is a compile error, not a crash at run time.
cards/5/q: A window with a centered button
cards/5/explain: Avalonia has no Middle. The center is called Center.
cards/6/q: Match each markup piece to what it means
cards/6/pairs/3/1: A field you can use from code
cards/7/q: What is true about AXAML? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/0: It is compiled at build time
cards/7/options/1: Any markup can be rewritten as C# code
cards/7/options/3: It runs as a script in the browser
cards/7/explain: XAML turns into ordinary code at compile time.
cards/8/q: A Window has a single Content property. How do you put several elements in a window?
cards/8/options/0: Put a panel (StackPanel, Grid...) in the window, and the elements in the panel
cards/8/explain: Panels lay out their children. That is the next unit.
